land.text: the Tuoba, who 'in 258 ... settled near the frontier and occupied the abandoned city of Shengle' (near modern Hohhot)

predecessors.note: The Xianbei confederation fell apart after Kebineng's murder in 235 (Xianbei page); the Tuoba had moved to the Yin Mountains earlier and Liwei absorbed a local tribe in 248. The land at Shengle was an abandoned Han city, so nobody held it in 258.

land.text: the Tuoba lands north of the mountain ranges that Yilu, Duke of Dai from 310, held: the Tuoba state continued under the Jin title of Dai

successors.note: Same people, same core: Tuoba Yilu was appointed Duke of Dai by the Western Jin in 310 and the Dai page dates the state 310-376. The dai-sixteen-kingdoms dossier does not list this dossier as predecessor (it names western-jin only) and uses family china; the colour agent should consider one colour for both (rule 2).

capitals.name: Shengle (near Hohhot)
capitals.note: Xianbei page: 'The Tuoba later built their capital at Shengle near modern Hohhot'; the Tuoba Liwei page calls Shengle only an occupied base in Dingxiang Commandery. Coordinates are a point near Hohhot, approximate; the page gives no coordinates.

correction.text: 'In 258, the Tuoba tribe settled near the frontier and occupied the abandoned city of Shengle, north of the Yin Mountains' (near modern Hohhot); Liwei's earlier base along the Chang River (Xinghe County) lies at the edge of this disc

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria shape; the Xianbei row ends 237 and nothing covers the steppe after). The pages give a city and a base, not a boundary or an area, so the disc is a core, not the extent. Shengle is in Dingxiang Commandery (Tuoba Liwei page). No infobox area exists to compare.

correction.text: in 295 Tuoba Luguan 'divided the territory under Tuoba control into three areas'; the western area ran 'west from White Mountain (northeast of Zhangjiakou), to Dai (Datong, Shanxi)', and Shengle (south of Hohhot) lay in another area

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page names only the western area and does not say where the other two lay or who held Shengle; the union of the Shengle core and the Zhangjiakou-Datong belt is a reading. Luguan's three-way split and Yilu's reunification in 307 do not change the outer shape. No area is given.

region.text: the abandoned Han city of Shengle, north of the Yin Mountains, near modern Hohhot

ledger.note: 258: the Tuoba under Tuoba Liwei occupy the abandoned city of Shengle near Hohhot. 'In 258, the Tuoba tribe settled near the frontier and occupied the abandoned city of Shengle, north of the Yin Mountains.' The Tuoba Liwei page says he led his followers to 'occupy the abandoned Han city of Shengle' in Dingxiang Commandery. The page gives the city, not a boundary; the disc is the researcher's reading. Earlier, in 248, Liwei 'killed the chieftain of the local tribe and absorbed them into his following' (Xianbei page).

region.text: the western area from White Mountain (northeast of Zhangjiakou) to Dai (Datong, Shanxi)

ledger.note: 295: the Tuoba domain stands from Zhangjiakou to Datong when Luguan divides it in three. The Tuoba Yilu page dates the division (295; the Dai page says 294) and names the western area but is silent on when or from whom the belt between Shengle and Datong was taken, so the gain is placed at the division year as a bridge.

region.text: the Tuoba lands round Shengle and Dai

ledger.note: 310: the Western Jin invest Tuoba Yilu as Duke of Dai, and the Tuoba state carries on as Dai (dai-sixteen-kingdoms). 'Tuoba Yilu was appointed the Duke of Dai (代公) by the Western Jin dynasty in 310', infobox 'Established: 310'. The dossier ends in 309 so that the Dai dossier's found event at 310 takes the land without an overlap year; the five counties Yilu was granted are in the Dai ledger.

wars.name: Tuoba and Jin campaign against Liu Yuan's Han (Han-Zhao)
wars.outcome: Yilu and Yituo 'joined forces with the Jin armies and defeated Liu Yuan' in 304; no border moved.
wars.note: The Dai page: the Tuoba chiefs 'cooperated with each other to provide Jin with cavalry support'. Listed so the reviewer can see it was considered; the Jin grants of 310 and 315 are in the Dai dossier.

certainty.note: A tribal union on the steppe frontier: the pages give a city (Shengle), a base on the Chang River and the western belt from White Mountain to Dai, never a boundary line.

notes: Requested by the p0200-p0299 window (the xianbei dossier's successors point to this slug). The Tuoba are a tribal union, not a state with borders: the pages give Shengle (near Hohhot), a base on the Chang River and a western belt from White Mountain to Dai, and no area, so the dossier draws a core and a belt, soft, and is honest that the 258-294 extent is unknown. Range 258-309 is chosen so that the Tuoba do not overlap dai-sixteen-kingdoms (310-376), which is the same people under a Jin title; the colour agent should consider one colour for both. The dossier gives no rulers because the pages date only Liwei (to 277), Luguan (294-307) and Yilu (307-316) and leave 277-294 unnamed. Relations the neighbours' dossiers should carry: Tuoba hostage to Cao Wei in 261 (Tuoba Liwei page: Liwei sent his son Shamohan to Luoyang) and Western Jin investiture in 310/315 (Dai page); the 258 Shengle lies in what had been Han Dingxiang Commandery (nobody's in 258). Not settled: Liwei's death in 277 and the chiefs scattering on a rumour (Tuoba Liwei page) probably shrank the union to 294, but no page dates a loss; the Tuoba page itself dates the Dai state 310-376 and the table has Yituo and Yilu from 295. Wikidata id not known (wikidata.org unreachable). Duan Liaoxi (the other half of the p0200 request) already exists as duan-liaoxi.json, and that dossier lists tuoba-xianbei as the missing slug in xianbei's successors. Gazetteer names used: Hohhot, Datong, Zhangjiakou (all in places.jsonl).
